newsitem.title: USA: Forecasters see below avg temps for U.S. Northeast.
newsitem.headline: Forecasters see below avg temps for U.S. Northeast.

text.p: The U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world, will experience much below normal temperatures by late week and into next week, weather forecasters said.
"The eastern one third of the nation will have temperatures in the range of 10 to 20 degrees below normal from Friday to Monday," said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis in Chicago.

Davis said the cold airmass is a piece of arctic air positioned over Alaska and the Northwest Territories during the past 10 days, and part of it will reach Texas and the Midwest, including Chicago, by Thursday.

Davis said the cold front could possibly cause disruptions of energy operations along the U.S. Gulf Coast and disruptions in Mexican oil operations in the Bay of Campeche due to strong winds and high seas.
Freese-Notis Weather, a private forecaster in Des Moines, Iowa, expected temperatures in parts of the Northeast to drop eight to 10 degrees below normal between January 12 and 16.

"Our six to 10 day forecast calls for below normal temperatures from the Rockies to the East Coast. It will be cold in the Northeast but not as cold as in the Midwest where it may get brutally cold," said meteorologist Charlie Notis.
The National Weather Service's six-to-10 day forecast called for normal to below normal temperatures in the Northeast.
Weather Services Corp expected Northeast temperatures to be five to 10 degrees below normal Tuesday and Wednesday and three to six degrees below normal Thursday and Friday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
